steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest closes on Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. Madrid (CET/CEST) is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time (PT) on that date (Madrid will be on CET, UTC+1, as Daylight Saving Time ends on October 25, 2026, while PT is UTC-8). Adding 9 hours to 11:59 PM PT on October 30 means the time rolls over to the next day.

11:59 PM PT on October 30 + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on October 31.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time (PDT, UTC-7). Madrid (CET, UTC+1) is 8 hours ahead of Los Angeles. Adding 8 hours to 10:00 AM gives 6:00 PM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 Madrid time. Since it lasts exactly 48 hours, which is two full days, it will end at the same time two days later.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The final round starts on October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT. Submissions close exactly 72 hours later, which is October 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT.
On October 29, 2026, Pacific Time (PT) will be PDT (UTC-7) as US Daylight Saving Time ends on November 1st. Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) as European Daylight Saving Time ends on October 25th.
The time difference between Madrid (UTC+1) and PDT (UTC-7) is +8 hours (Madrid is 8 hours ahead).
Therefore, 10:00 AM PT on October 29, 2026, is 10:00 AM + 8 hours = 6:00 PM (18:00) in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Submissions close at October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. On this date, Eastern Time (ET) in the US refers to Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.
So, 11:59 PM EDT on October 31, 2026, is 19:59 UTC on October 31, 2026.

The results are announced exactly 36 hours after this.
19:59 UTC on October 31, 2026 + 36 hours = 07:59 UTC on November 2, 2026.

For Madrid, Spain: European Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, this is October 25. Therefore, on November 2, 2026, Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.

Converting 07:59 UTC to Madrid local time (CET):
07:59 UTC + 1 hour = 08:59 CET on November 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 08:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The Unix timestamp 1791788340 corresponds to 2026-11-20 03:00:00 UTC.
Tokyo's local time is Japan Standard Time (JST), which is UTC+9.
Adding 9 hours to 03:00:00 UTC gives 12:00:00 JST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-20 12:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 during standard time, and Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2 during daylight saving time. Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, this is October 25th. The change occurs at 03:00 CEST, when clocks go back to 02:00 CET.

The deadline is 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z.
02:30 UTC on October 25th is *after* the daylight saving time change (which happens at 01:00 UTC, equivalent to 03:00 CEST becoming 02:00 CET). Therefore, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1) at this time.

02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026.
On this date, Pacific Time will still be Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7, as Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on the first Sunday of November.
In Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October. Therefore, on October 25, 2026, Madrid will switch from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1). By 11:59 PM PDT, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

Madrid (CET, UTC+1) is 8 hours ahead of PDT (UTC-7).
So, 11:59 PM PDT on October 25, 2026, plus 8 hours, is 7:59 AM on October 26, 2026, in Madrid local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The US ends Daylight Saving Time on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, this is November 1st. On this day, at 2:00 AM, Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) switches to Eastern Standard Time (EST, UTC-5). The deadline of "12:00 noon Eastern Time" on that day refers to 12:00 PM EST. Lima, Peru, observes Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5. Since both EST and PET are UTC-5, the time will be the same in both locations.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) typically refers to the last time zone on Earth, which is UTC-12. "December 31, 2026, 24:00" is equivalent to "January 1, 2027, 00:00" in that time zone (UTC-12). Tokyo is UTC+9. To find the time in Tokyo, we add 21 hours (9 - (-12) = 21) to the UTC-12 time.

January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC-12 + 21 hours = January 1, 2027, 21:00 UTC+9 (Tokyo time).

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney (AEDT) is UTC+11 on October 5, 2026, and New York (EDT) is UTC-4. This means Sydney is 15 hours ahead of New York. To find the New York time, subtract 15 hours from the Sydney deadline of 5:00 PM (17:00) on October 5, 2026. 17:00 - 15 hours = 02:00. The date remains the same.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
